seven_facts_commentary.headline: 29 subjects. 29 / 26 / 21 / 21 / 15 / 21 / 13. SEVEN DIFFERENT NUMBERS, AND THE FALL FROM 29 TO 13 IS THE PRODUCT OF THIS AUDIT.
seven_facts_commentary.authored_29: AUTHORED = 29 of 29. Every subject in the measured census has a plugin, a store and handlers on disk. NOT ONE FINDING IN THIS AUDIT IS 'THE CAPABILITY DOES NOT EXIST'. That is the single most important sentence here, because it determines the disposition of every remediation: of 27 findings, 10 are WIRE, 9 REPLACE, 6 DOCUMENT and only 2 REMOVE. TWO OF THE 29 ARE AUTHORED IN CODE BUT NOT AS AN L0 RECORD -- lift and liftPart carry a hand-written z.object at L2 instead of a defineElement, which is why the schema census reads 30 kinds while the family census reads 29 subjects.
seven_facts_commentary.dispatchable_26: DISPATCHABLE = 26. THE THREE THAT ARE NOT ARE NOT BROKEN -- TWO OF THEM ARE DELIBERATELY REFUSING. door.create (CreateDoor.ts:154) and window.create (CreateWindow.ts:98) refuse EVERY well-formed payload BY CONSTRUCTION, because the real opening path is wall.opening.create and the repo chose to make the rivals refuse rather than leave two write paths. Reading this drop as a defect would restore the rival. The third, selection, is a genuine total dispatch failure sitting behind a green plugin suite. USER MEANING: 26 is the right number and the gap is a design decision in two cases out of three.
seven_facts_commentary.reachable_21: REACHABLE = 21. THE FIVE-FAMILY DROP FROM DISPATCHABLE IS THE FIRST REAL ONE, and it is where the product stops answering a gesture. grid, structural, dimension, section-view and slab each have a schema, a store, a handler and a CommandEventBridge case -- and no user gesture arrives at them, or arrives and lands nowhere. dimension is the sharpest: dimensionTool is READ at PluginRegistry.ts:1051 and ASSIGNED NOWHERE, so the 'not ready -- engine not yet initialised' branch is PERMANENT rather than a startup race. slab is different and worse in one way: it IS reached, but slab.create {boundary} -- a shape the payload type accepts and PreviewManager.ts:333 actually sends -- lands in no authoritative store. USER MEANING: the user clicks, the app reports success, and nothing exists. A successful creation and a silent refusal are the same number of pixels. TWO SUBJECTS (ceiling, curtain-wall) are UNVERIFIED here rather than NO -- there is no authoritative store to read back from, so the honest answer is 'not measurable headlessly', not 'broken'.
seven_facts_commentary.renders_3d_21: RENDERS 3D = 21 -- the SAME 21 as reachable, and the identity is not a coincidence. In this codebase, reaching the authoritative store and appearing in the viewport are the same event: the store's add() emits, and a builder listens. Nothing in the measured set reaches a store and then fails to draw. USER MEANING: the 3-D viewport is the honest surface. If a family arrives in the store, the user sees it. What the number hides is FIDELITY, not presence -- roof drops materialId and materialColor through the bridge (B2-ROOF-01) and still counts as YES, because the seven-fact chain HAS NO FIDELITY AXIS. A family can read 7/7 while silently discarding the user's material choice.
seven_facts_commentary.renders_plan_15: RENDERS PLAN = 15. THE NARROWEST FACT IN THE AUDIT, AND THE SIX-SUBJECT DROP FROM 3-D IS THE MOST USER-VISIBLE GAP THE PRODUCT HAS. A BIM tool that draws in 3-D and not in plan is not a BIM tool -- plan is where drawings are issued. The mechanism is not one bug but a membership list: GEOMETRY_ELEMENT_TYPES (ViewDependencyTracker.ts:42-49). 'room', 'lighting', 'water', 'liftPart', 'balcony' and 'boundaryLine' are absent from it in one spelling or another. The consequences differ in kind: liftPart and the pool's water body have NO plan symbol builder at all (the cabin and the water simply are not drawn); lighting's bridge calls bimManager but NOT viewDependencyTracker -- the ONE bridge of fifteen calling half the pair, so a light is enumerable but not dirty-markable; slab fails plan for exactly the payload shapes that fail 3-D, because VDT (:2400) and bimManager (:2401) both sit downstream of the same `!ev.polygon || !ev.id` early return. FOUR SUBJECTS ARE UNVERIFIED HERE and one (water) is DISPUTED between the family row and the adversarial pass -- this is the least settled column in the table and the one most worth a browser probe. A CRITICAL CORRECTION TO THE AUDIT'S OWN METHOD: the brief's rule 'missing EITHER registerElement means exportForView returns 0 elements' IS TOO STRONG. exportForView's PLAN branch builds its set from levels.flatMap(l => l.childrenIds) -- bimManager ONLY. viewDependencyTracker feeds targeted dirty-marking; its absence DEGRADES to the S-G3-STALE fallback, it does not empty the export. And plan SYMBOL injection (EdgeProjectorService.ts:3936) is a SIBLING of the mesh loop, not a child, so door, window, furniture and plumbing plan symbols do not require the family to be in childrenIds at all. Three admissible mechanisms, not one.
seven_facts_commentary.persists_21: PERSISTS = 21, and this column contains the audit's single most dangerous finding. THE NUMBER IS NOT THE POINT -- THE SILENCE IS. balcony reads persists=NO through a channel that DOES NOT EXIST on the composed runtime (ProjectSerializer.ts:1519 reads window.runtime.stores.balcony; composeRuntime's StoresSlot has no balcony key and no index signature), while snapshotFamilyCoverage.ts:161 DECLARES it status:'persisted' -- so balcony is not in UNPERSISTED_FAMILY_KEYS and the C84 EI-6 loss loop NEVER NAMES IT. A user authors a balcony, sees it drawn, is told the project saved, and the balcony is gone on reload with no console line. boundary-line is the same shape one layer along: the SAVE half works and the RESTORE sits in the legacy branch of a default-false path (ProjectLoader.ts:765 / _useImportCommandPath returns TRUE by default), so the data is written into the file and never read back. SAVED AND NEVER RESTORED IS STRICTLY WORSE THAN NEVER SAVED. Contrast the THREE HONEST LOSSES -- bathroomPod (L-11527), section-view (L-11524), structural (L-11523) -- which are DECLARED and which the gate names at baseline 3. A declared loss is a product decision; an undeclared one is data destruction. And the gate that blesses all of this exits 0: 'NOT ESTABLISHED HERE: that any family ROUND-TRIPS.'
seven_facts_commentary.exports_13: EXPORTS = 13 of 29 -- LESS THAN HALF, AND IT IS THE END OF THE CHAIN FOR TWICE AS MANY FAMILIES AS ANY OTHER FACT. USER MEANING: the model is richer than anything the user can hand to a consultant. Annotations and dimensions do not export AT ALL, so a sheet exported to PDF carries no dimensions -- a documentation family whose entire purpose does not survive the export. Floor finishes, ceilings, balconies, pools, water, lifts and boundary lines are all absent from IFC. THE COLUMN IS ALSO THE AUDIT'S OWN WORST-MEASURED ONE, and the reason is instructive: TWO EXPORTERS EXIST FOR ONE CONCEPT. packages/file-format/src/export/ifc (the one the Export IFC button runs, via initUI.ts) carries per-family Readers including Furniture and Plumbing; plugins/ifc-export/src/exporters/IFC4X3Exporter.ts reads snapshot.walls/slabs/doors/windows/columns/beams/rooms only. Two family rows searched only the plugin subtree and reported NO for families that DO export -- a search by DIRECTORY NAME rather than by CAPABILITY. The floor row, which enumerated the right directory, is the control case, and its own printed listing contained the FurnitureReader and PlumbingReader that refuted its siblings. The refuting evidence was already inside this audit. CRUCIALLY: 14 families read exports=NO and THERE IS NO SINGLE PLACE THAT SAYS WHICH OF THOSE 14 ARE INTENTIONAL. A setting-out line arguably should not be an IfcElement; a dimension certainly should reach a PDF.
seven_facts_commentary.the_gaps_together: READ THE SEVEN AS A DESCENT AND THE PRODUCT'S SHAPE APPEARS: 29 authored -> 26 dispatchable (2 refusals BY DESIGN, 1 real failure) -> 21 reachable (5 gestures that go nowhere) -> 21 in 3D (the viewport is honest: what reaches the store is drawn) -> 15 in plan (the drawing surface is the narrowest, and a BIM tool is judged there) -> 21 persisting (the number RISES, which is the tell: some families that never draw still save, and two that draw perfectly do not survive reload) -> 13 exporting (the model outruns the deliverable by more than 2:1). THE RISE FROM 15 TO 21 BETWEEN PLAN AND PERSIST IS THE SINGLE MOST DIAGNOSTIC MOVEMENT IN THE TABLE. These are not one pipeline with a leak at a known point; they are seven independent memberships -- a CEB case, a tool activation, a GEOMETRY_ELEMENT_TYPES row, a bimManager registration, a StoresSlot key, a snapshot field, an IFC Reader -- and a family is in each or not, independently. THAT is why the numbers do not match and why no single fix moves more than one of them.
seven_facts_commentary.what_the_brief_got_wrong: THE BRIEF'S OWN HEADLINE OVER-REPORTED THREE GAPS, AND EVERY ONE OF THE THREE PROPOSED FIXES WAS WORSE THAN THE MEASURED STATE. G1 named EIGHT dispatchable-but-invisible families; FIVE (room, plumbing, annotation, balcony, pool) are reached, each by a mechanism 'has an own-name initTools bridge' cannot see -- member re-stamping onto members' channels, a store-driven plan symbol builder that never consults childrenIds, a separate render subsystem. G2 called water 'a bridge listening for an event nothing emits'; the emitter is CommandEventBridge.ts:2051 inside `case 'pool.create'`, and water owns no verb DELIBERATELY (ADR-0124 S4) -- actioning G2 would have deleted a live render bridge or minted the exact rival the ADR forbids. G3's premise that liftPart and bathroomPod are schema-less compound MEMBERS is half wrong: bathroomPod is a compound PARENT owning two verbs. D2 is not a stylistic preference. Three of the brief's own findings were name-shaped searches, and the fix each one implied would have made the product worse.
